solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Throw conductor

definitions.meaning: to throw someone is to unnerve or fluster them
Sir Simon ... is a famous British orchestral conductor

explanation.definitionFit: To rattle a person is to disconcert them, and Simon Rattle led the Berlin Philharmonic and London Symphony orchestras.

clue.text: See 10 across
Avenue may be entered — maybe £1 to enter

indicators.note: to enter tells us the pound sign and figure one go inside the reworked letters
maybe suggests the letters of the word entered could be arranged otherwise

parts.note: the pound sign is L (from Latin libra) and the figure 1 looks like I

explanation.surface: A statement that an avenue may be entered, perhaps on payment of a pound toll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Avenue may be' is an adjectival definition: some avenues have trees along both sides. The pound sign is L from Latin libra; the anagram gives TREENED.
explanation.definitionFit: Many avenues are bordered by rows of planted trees along each side.

clue.text: Period of brilliance

definitions.meaning: a ..., or lustrum, is a span of five years
shine or sheen, as on polished metal

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a dated term for a five-year span and the ordinary word for gleam or radiance.

clue.text: Laboratory substance caught by one in border state

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: in places the letter for one inside the border-and-state pair

parts.note: a hem is the border of a garment
CAL is short for California, a US state
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A dangerous lab compound seized at a frontier by a single officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Compounds and reagents handled in a lab are chemicals.

clue.text: May put me with confidence among the ancient

indicators.note: among places me and confidence inside the word for ancient

parts.note: hoary means very old
taken as written
a confidence is a secret told in trust

explanation.surface: Someone may share a secret with me among the old folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' is not the month or a verb: Theresa May held this UK cabinet post (minister for policing and immigration) before becoming Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Theresa May served in this British cabinet office from 2010 to 2016.

clue.text: Holy word repeated quietly to catch trespassers

parts.note: a mantra is a sacred word or phrase chanted over and over
P stands for piano, the musical direction for softly

explanation.surface: Someone chants a sacred word softly in the hope of catching intruders.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-trap is a device, often a sprung jaw, set to seize intruders on private land.

clue.text: Plants that function in the Channel Islands

indicators.note: in places the function word inside the islands abbreviation

parts.note: CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands, Jersey and Guernsey off France
to act is to function or operate

explanation.surface: Greenery that works well on Jersey and Guernsey.
explanation.definitionFit: Succulent spiny desert plants of the family Cactaceae.

clue.text: Stay that is missing from underwear

indicators.note: missing from says the abbreviation for that is is taken out of the underwear word

parts.note: lingerie is women's underwear
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A remark about something absent from a set of undergarments.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay on is to remain or loiter.

clue.text: Cupboard for papers

definitions.meaning: a large cupboard, especially for linen or clothes

explanation.definitionFit: A press is a tall storage cupboard, and the same word names newspapers and journalists as a body.

clue.text: Note small container at inn in survival of half an island

parts.note: do (or doh) is a note in tonic sol-fa
mini means small
a can is a container

indicators.note: in puts the inn word inside the survival word

parts.note: a relic is something surviving from the past
a pub is an inn

explanation.surface: A tale of a musical note and a tiny tin found at a pub among ancient remains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is only a link. The definition is fair because the country shares the island of Hispaniola with Haiti.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caribbean nation occupies the eastern part of Hispaniola, Haiti the western part.

clue.text: Made out instructions for liturgy, achieving award

parts.note: to make out is to discern or tell apart
here the words are taken in the other sequence

explanation.surface: Someone read the church programme and won a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'achieving' is a link. The DSO is a British military decoration for officers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Distinguished Service Order is a British military decoration for officers.

clue.text: Country left between Russia (so called) and America

indicators.note: between places the letter for left inside the national-animal word

parts.note: Russia is often called the Bear, its national symbol
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A nation lying between Russia and America on the political left.
explanation.definitionFit: Belarus is a landlocked Eastern European nation bordering Poland and Ukraine.

clue.text: See 10 down
See 19
Record that is long-playing played by student

parts.note: a disc is a record

indicators.note: played signals that the abbreviations are reworked

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A student puts on a long-playing record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is only a link; 'played' works on the two abbreviations together, giving IPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A disciple is a follower or pupil of a teacher.

clue.text: Back trouble without consent had got cosmetic

indicators.note: without means outside, so the reversed word surrounds the rest
Back says the trouble word is read the other way round

parts.note: woe is trouble or misery
yes signals consent
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone with a bad back got a cosmetic treatment without agreeing to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense of outside, not lacking; the reversed trouble word is EOW. 'got' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A make-up product applied to the eyelids.

clue.text: Harp cult exploited by ancient historian

indicators.note: exploited suggests the letters are worked over and reorganised

explanation.surface: A Greek writer takes advantage of a cult of harp players.
explanation.definitionFit: Plutarch was a Greek biographer of the first century AD, author of the Parallel Lives.

clue.text: Fashionable symbol among animals

indicators.note: among puts the symbol word inside the animals word

parts.note: deer are animals
a sign is a symbol

explanation.surface: A trendy emblem seen among a herd of creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Designer goods carry a famous label and are stylish and expensive.

clue.text: Philosopher's watering place (including in Australia)

indicators.note: including says the spa word holds the other letters

parts.note: a spa is a resort with medicinal springs
taken as written
Oz is a nickname for Australia

explanation.surface: A thinker's favourite resort, with one down under.
explanation.definitionFit: Baruch Spinoza was a seventeenth-century Dutch rationalist thinker.

clue.text: Marine creatures authenticate charged items

parts.note: to seal a document is to authenticate it
ions are electrically charged particles

explanation.surface: Someone certifies a batch of goods that have been billed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea lions are eared seals of Pacific coasts.

clue.text: Visit by physician and most of what he says?

parts.note: Dr is short for doctor

indicators.note: most of means the last few letters of the word are lopped off

parts.note: a doctor gives an opinion

explanation.surface: A house call by a doctor, and nearly everything he tells you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' cuts ION from OPINION, leaving OPIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop in is to pay a casual call.

clue.text: Enthusiasm averred to 'ave more difficulty?

indicators.note: averred means stated, and the dropped H in 'ave shows the word is spoken by someone who drops aitches

parts.note: harder means with more difficulty; with the H dropped it is said 'arder

explanation.surface: Someone claims to be keener on having a tougher time.
explanation.walkthrough: In a Cockney accent, which drops H as in 'ave for have, harder comes out sounding like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardour is passion or eager zeal.

clue.text: Composer's son involved with Iris

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters are tangled up together

explanation.surface: A musician's boy gets mixed up with a girl called Iris.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini was the Italian who wrote The Barber of Seville.

clue.text: Pursuer of nymph or nymphalid

definitions.meaning: in Greek myth these woodland goat-men chase nymphs
a brown butterfly of the family Nymphalidae

explanation.definitionFit: A satyr is a lustful woodland spirit of myth and also a brown butterfly in the brush-footed family.

clue.text: Costly miss top class? Don't talk nonsense about it

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with the figure 1 read as I

indicators.note: about means the nonsense word goes round the hush word

parts.note: rot is nonsense
sh is a call for silence

explanation.surface: A first-rate player is told to stop talking rubbish about an expensive blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is a link. In cricket or golf an air shot is a swing that misses the ball entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: A swing in golf or cricket that connects with nothing but air, often costing a stroke or wicket.

clue.text: Shame about lake and river: it's on the Tummel

indicators.note: about means the shame word goes around the others

parts.note: a pity is a shame
loch is the Scottish word for a lake

explanation.surface: A regret about a Scottish loch and river beside a Highland town.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitlochry is a Perthshire town on the River Tummel in Scotland.

clue.text: See 10 down
Two little boys over the water

parts.note: Norm is short for the boy's name Norman
Andy is short for the boy's name Andrew

explanation.surface: A pair of small lads crossing a river.
explanation.walkthrough: From England, the French region lies across the Channel, hence 'over the water'.
explanation.definitionFit: The French region lies across the English Channel from southern England.

clue.text: Blazing row that conceals economic panacea

indicators.note: conceals says the letters lie inside the run of words before it

explanation.surface: A fiery argument hides the cure-all economists want.
explanation.definitionFit: Economic expansion is touted as the remedy for all fiscal ills.
